title: Follow-ups: the Orders, Inbox and abandoned-checkout answers, the inventory and email sets and the read scheduler say only what they actually read
requested_outcome:
Eight follow-ups from the round-12 deploy review, filed as work for the next build under the owner's ship rule of 30 September. Each is a read that answers the owner with more certainty than it has. The rule for all of them: say only what was read; when a read was cut short or limited to a window, the spoken words and the card say so (or the read covers the whole scope). Fix each with a test that fails on the code at the base commit.
- F/F-02 (app/families/landings.py _orders_plan/_orders_render; app/families/summaries.py LOOKBACK_DAYS, commerce_summary): the Orders landing searches only last_30_days yet can say 'Nothing is waiting to go out'; an unqualified orders_attention summary searches 90 days. An older unfulfilled order is absent from both answers.
- F/F-03 (app/families/landings.py _inbox_plan/_recent_render): the recent-inbox read asks for at most 12 threads, yet can say 'Nothing from a person in the inbox this week' when those 12 are bulk mail and a person's thread is further back; the empty branch also drops result.partial.
- F/F-04 (app/families/abandoned.py ABANDONED_QUERY, _lines, rank, cards): each abandoned checkout fetches only its first 20 line items, and the item ranking is presented as complete; an item always 21st is never counted.
- AC1/AC1-NEW-01 (app/tools/analytics_tools.py inventory_query, _run, _set_from): max_days_cover is applied after the working set was made and attached, so 'these' holds variants the rows left out.
- AC1-F-01 (round 10, ruled still present at round 12; app/tools/analytics_tools.py email_query, look): a customer whose record has no email address is answered available: True with no threads, so it is counted as checked and put in not_contacted.
- S5/S5-02 (app/reads/scheduler.py _layers and run_plan's runnable check): a read whose after names a read the plan does not hold runs anyway, against the scheduler's own guarantee that a missing dependency is skipped.
- S5/S5-03 (app/anticipation/engine.py on_signal, forget): positions are kept under 'scope|branch_id' but forget(scope) removes only 'scope', so an ended conversation keeps them and can feed a false transition.
- R9-I-tests5-I-02 (round 9, ruled still present at round 12; tests/test_turn_surfaces.py): the returning-customers test compares the drawn patch types as a set, so two summary cards staged in one turn would pass it.
Landings stay the fixed reads a tap names; nothing here reads the owner's words to decide what to read.

What must not change, in every part of this build: every sentence the owner types or says still goes to the model exactly as said, and nothing here reads, answers or routes a sentence by a word list in front of it (deterministic code may check what the model did, never decide for it); every change to the shop or to email stays behind the owner's hold-to-confirm card, nothing here adds a write or skips staging, confirmation or verification, and reads stay reads; no private business data goes into git, and every name, address and order in a test is invented; no test assertion is weakened (an assertion changed here is made stricter, and the report names each one); the kernel, the gate, secret scanning and the acceptance machinery are untouched, and no protected path is edited (protected tests such as tests/test_compose.py, tests/test_engineering_bridge.py and tests/conftest.py are run, never changed); docs/phase4/TOOL_MATRIX.md is regenerated by the loop and never edited by hand. Plain British English in comments and docstrings that say what is true and why; no placeholder copy, invented defaults or filler.

DIRECTOR'S NOTES FROM REVIEWING THE PREVIOUS CANDIDATE (93a19e92, which stopped at the repair limit). If the branch clive/objective/followups-reads-say-what-they-read is in your workspace, its last commit is a near-complete version; these must also hold:
(1) F-03 must hold against the REAL gmail_search, not a test shape. gmail_search lists the 12 newest MESSAGES, drops bulk mail before returning (include_bulk defaults to False and the landing does not pass it) and folds what is left to one entry per thread, so a thread count of 12 almost never happens. app/tools/gmail_tools.py is now in scope for exactly this: gmail_search's result carries "listed": how many messages the list returned. The landing decides the read was cut short on body['listed'] >= RECENT_LIMIT, words the answer as among 'the 12 newest emails', and marks it partial; its tests build their input through gmail_search itself with the message listing faked (11 bulk + 1 person; 12 bulk; one 6-message thread + 6 others), never a hand-built thread list.
(2) F-02's card: when the 360-day read failed or came back incomplete and nothing in the last 30 days is waiting, the Orders landing still draws a card saying nothing in the window is waiting and older orders could not be checked; when orders are waiting and the older read is incomplete, the 30-day card is marked incomplete. Never zero cards.
(3) When orders older than 30 days and older than 360 days are both present, the count and 'the oldest' in the first sentence cover them all, so the next sentence never names an older order than 'the oldest'.
(4) With zero orders considered, the note never says 'Read from the 0 orders'.
acceptance_criteria: F-02: with a fake shop holding an unfulfilled order older than 30 days (and one older than 90), the Orders landing either lists it, or its words and its card say the window that was read and never the bare 'Nothing is waiting to go out'; commerce_summary's unqualified orders_attention does the same for its lookback. A shop with no open order at all still gets the plain answer.

F-03: when the inbox read came back at its thread limit and every thread was bulk, the answer does not say nobody wrote this week: it says how many recent threads were checked (or the read pages until the week is covered); the empty answer is partial whenever the read was partial.

F-04: a checkout with more than 20 line items, whose item past the twentieth is on no other checkout, either has that item counted (its lines paged) or the ranking is marked incomplete on the card and in the words.

AC1-NEW-01: inventory_query(max_days_cover=N) attaches a working set whose members are exactly the returned rows' variants (none with cover above N or unknown), with its count, label and totals matching those rows.

AC1-F-01: in email_query a customer with no email address is neither in not_contacted nor counted there; the counts say how many had no address (or count them with the unchecked), and the set a later 'the rest' would act on excludes them.
S5-02: a plan holding a read whose after names a missing read never dispatches it; the result lists it as skipped with a reason, and a read that depends on it is skipped too.
S5-03: after signals on two halves of one conversation, forget(scope) leaves no position for either half, and the next signal on either learns no transition from before the forget.

R9-I-tests5-I-02: the returning-customers test in tests/test_turn_surfaces.py asserts the drawn patches are exactly one summary_list (a list compared, not a set) and still passes; the assertion is stricter, not weaker.

The new tests are in tests/test_followups_reads.py, each failing on the base code; the neighbouring families, summaries, analytics, reads and anticipation tests and tests/test_r13_evidence_index.py still pass.

Driving the real gmail_search (message listing faked) into the landing: 11 bulk + 1 person, 12 bulk, and one 6-message thread + 6 others each give an answer marked partial and worded as among the 12 newest emails, with a card that says so.
The Orders landing never draws zero cards: with the 360-day read failed or incomplete and nothing waiting in 30 days it draws one saying older orders could not be checked.
No sentence names an order older than the one the answer calls the oldest.
